question: You are asked to perform amniotomy (ARM) in a woman at 41 weeks in active labour. Which of the following is an ABSOLUTE contraindication to performing ARM at this point?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. A cervix dilated to 4 cm is accessible and ARM is routinely performed at this dilatation. ARM at 4 cm in active labour is a common practice to accelerate progress.

Correct. Cord presentation (funic presentation) is an absolute contraindication to ARM. Rupturing membranes with a presenting cord risks cord prolapse, umbilical cord compression, and acute fetal compromise. Immediate caesarean section is required.
Incorrect. A Bishop score of 7 indicates a favourable cervix, and ARM is usually appropriate in this setting when induction or augmentation is planned.
Incorrect. A vertex at 0 station (level of ischial spines) is an engaged, presenting vertex and is a prerequisite for safe ARM, not a contraindication.

overallFeedback.feedback: Key ARM contraindications: cord presentation or prolapse, vasa praevia, unengaged head (floating), malpresentation at the os, active genital herpes. ARM in any of these risks immediate fetal compromise.

Correct. Cord presentation is an absolute contraindication to ARM. Other contraindications include vasa praevia, unengaged head (risk of cord prolapse), active herpes simplex infection, HIV with high viral load, and face presentation.
